title: The Albedos, Sizes, Colors, and Satellites of Dwarf Planets Compared with Newly Measured Dwarf Planet 2013 FY27
question: What are the size, albedo, color and satellite properties of the dwarf planet 2013 FY27, and how do they compare with other large TNOs?

what.value: Phase integral q = 0.336 pV + 0.479 for TNOs

evidence.quote: As shown in Brown & Butler (2017), $q$ for TNOs can be approximated by $0.336p_V + 0.479$.

what.value: Beaming parameter eta=1.175 and emissivity 0.70 for TNOs

evidence.quote: Lellouch et al. (2017) advise using a value of $\eta=1.175$ for TNOs observed with ALMA, so we adopt that value here.
using the transformation equations from Smith et al. (2002)

recipe.goal: Image ALMA continuum and measure flux
recipe.method: Calibrate with pipeline, combine three executions, natural-weighted continuum image, measure source flux
key_parameters: flux 25 microJy, rms 5.5 microJy, S/N about 4.5

recipe.goal: Optical photometry, colors, phase curve, absolute magnitude
recipe.method: Aperture photometry on Magellan g, r, i images; linear phase function from March and May r-band; transformation to V

recipe.goal: Solve size and albedo with NEATM
recipe.method: NEATM fit of thermal flux 25.0+-5.5 microJy at 3.075 mm and V=22.35+-0.03 for D and pV; errors at chi2=1
assumptions: Spherical, slow rotator, no nightside emission

evidence.quote: we find the optical color spectral slope is $S=17\pm 2$
The newly discovered satellite was $3.0\pm0.2$ mags fainter than the primary in the optical.

not_stated_but_needed: tclean parameters (cell size, image size, mask, niter, threshold)
how the source flux (25 microJy) was measured (peak vs fit)
spectral window setup and any flagging
calibrators other than J1127-1857 and J1058+0133 details
solar V magnitude and exact NEATM implementation code
score_reason: Simple recipe with ALMA data public, but imaging and flux extraction details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a single-flux numeric result, and a simple NEATM model make the main result reproducible.
